title: Unbelief
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Unbelief is the sinful refusal to trust God’s Word, goodness, promises, authority, and saving testimony in Christ. It is not merely intellectual doubt, but a heart posture that resists God.
summary: Unbelief is the sinful refusal to trust God’s Word, goodness, promises, authority, and saving testimony in Christ. It is not merely intellectual doubt, but a heart posture that resists God.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the One whom sinners are called to trust. He graciously receives weak faith, confronts hardened unbelief, and gives life to those who believe in Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Unbelief refuses God’s testimony. It may appear as rejection of the Gospel, refusal to obey, suspicion of God’s goodness, or resistance to His promises. Scripture treats unbelief as serious because it calls God untrustworthy.

Not all struggle is the same as hardened unbelief. Believers may battle questions, grief, weakness, or fear. Scripture shows a father crying, “I believe. Help my unbelief.” The Lord is merciful toward weak faith that comes to Him.

Unbelief becomes deadly when it hardens the heart against God. Israel’s wilderness rebellion shows that unbelief can persist even after seeing God’s works. The issue was not lack of evidence but refusal to trust and obey.

Christ calls sinners to believe. The written Word testifies to Him so that people may believe He is the Christ and have life in His name.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often treat unbelief as neutral or harmless, but Scripture shows that refusing God’s Word leads to disobedience, fear, rebellion, and judgment. The heart must not be allowed to harden.

This doctrine also helps tender believers distinguish weak faith from settled rejection. Those who bring their unbelief to Christ for help are not pushed away; they are called to trust His mercy and truth.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring doubts, fears, and unbelief honestly to Christ. Do not nurture suspicion of God or delay obedience while calling it caution. Hear the Word, ask for faith, trust the testimony of Scripture, and respond to Jesus with repentance and belief.
